"In Kuala Lumpur, the search for Indian tourist Vijaya Lakshmi Gali has been suspended after officials decided conditions were too dangerous for rescue crews. She vanished on 23 August when a pavement suddenly gave way beneath her, dropping her into a sinkhole about 8 metres deep. Since then, no sign of her has been found beyond her slippers.

***
Emergency teams used several advanced methods in hopes of locating her, including tracker dogs, remote cameras, and ground-penetrating radar. They also flushed parts of the underground drainage network with high-pressure water jets and brought in excavators to clear blocked material. Even with these efforts, the search reached its eighth day without a breakthrough.

***
* Officials said sending divers farther into the underground area was judged unsafe because of hazards to rescue staff, and an earlier attempt on Thursday had already shown how severe the danger was when two divers had to be pulled back before reaching an obstruction.

***
A minister in the prime minister’s department said the decision to halt the mission was based on the safety and health of personnel. This indicates that while authorities remain concerned about the missing tourist, they believe the underground setting now presents an unacceptable risk for anyone entering it.

***
The situation has also raised concern because authorities noted that a soil slip had been reported at the same location last year. That detail suggests the area may have had prior stability issues, adding to public alarm over the collapse and the difficult rescue effort. Is there anything else I can help with?"
